nodes.label: Weekly Supabase Backup to Telegram
nodes.rationale: The free Supabase tier has no automatic backups, and pet cards plus the Telegram-to-Altegio link exist nowhere else (Altegio has no animal records at all). The dump goes to Telegram rather than the PythonAnywhere disk: a copy on the same machine as the bot does not survive account problems, i.e. it fails to cover half the scenarios a backup exists for. api.telegram.org is already whitelisted on the proxy, Telegram keeps file history, so it costs nothing and adds no infrastructure. Format is one readable JSON file (jsonb and array columns would be flattened irreversibly by CSV), no gzip while the file stays in kilobytes.

nodes.label: Keyset Pagination of Table Reads
nodes.rationale: Reading by offset (.range()) defines the next window by how much was already read, so a row deleted between two requests (delete_pet, delete_pending_notifications_for_record from the Altegio webhook are real runtime deletions) shifts everything after it and one row silently misses the dump. Reading from the last key is immune, which is why the sort column must be unique and NOT NULL — nullable would give .gt(col, None) and an infinite loop. The loop exits on an empty page, not a short one: PAGE_SIZE is only our assumption about the PostgREST ceiling, and a smaller server-side db-max-rows would make 'short page' a false end-of-table signal, at the cost of one extra empty request per table.

nodes.label: Explicit BACKUP_TABLES Registry
nodes.rationale: Supabase REST cannot enumerate tables, so the list is a constant — with the useful side effect that adding a table forces a conscious decision about the backup, hence the post-migration checklist entry. It is a mapping table -> sort column rather than a plain list because there is no shared sort column: seven tables key on id, cron_state on the textual key. cron_state is included despite being operational state: four rows cost nothing and exclusion logic would be extra code.

nodes.label: Weekly Cadence Gating via cron_state
nodes.rationale: The weekly mark is the date of this week's Saturday rather than an ISO week number, because cron_state.last_run_date is a date column; Saturday and Sunday resolve to the same mark, so the Sunday catch-up (for when the external cron sleeps through Saturday) cannot fire twice. Hour 7 avoids 9 and 10 when other tasks message clients. The decision lives in the pure function is_backup_due(now, last_run, last_attempt) so the cadence is testable without mocking the scheduler; the dispatcher only writes marks. The success mark is written only after confirmed delivery.

nodes.label: Separate BACKUP_CHAT_ID Recipient
nodes.rationale: The dump carries client names and phone numbers, so it goes to the owner's private chat and must have no chance of landing in the shared staff group; the value lives only in .env and PythonAnywhere env vars, never as a default in config.py. Because the admin group is configured by a different variable, that channel is alive exactly when BACKUP_CHAT_ID is missing — which is the most likely production failure, so an unset variable notifies admins instead of only writing a log line nobody reads.

nodes.label: Loud Failure Principle
nodes.rationale: A backup that quietly stops working for half a year is worse than no backup — at least a missing one is known. Hence: any Supabase or Telegram failure logs and notifies the admin topic, the success mark is never written on failure, and the caption lists every table's row count including zeros (a review round removed the 'if n' filter, because a table that suddenly arrives empty from revoked rights or a rename would otherwise just vanish from the only artefact the owner actually reads).

nodes.label: Deliberately No Restore Script
nodes.rationale: It could only be verified against the live database (risking real data) or a separate test Supabase project, and an unverified restore script gives a false sense of safety. The full dump stays, and restore is written at the moment of need. Revisit if a test project appears. Encryption is also skipped: a password stored in the same private chat adds nothing.
